answer: Anchor each agent to a domain name, like a cedar rooted in one patch of ground. First, the agent registers a domain and posts a signed TXT record with its key. Second, it serves a live TLS certificate and answers a fresh challenge every 30 days. Third, the registry bars a second agent per domain and drops domains under 90 days old. Faking 1,000 identities means 1,000 domains at about $12 each plus 1,000 live sites kept up 3 months, roughly $36,000 a year before one fake earns a cent. A hollow shell of copy-paste identities fails, since each one needs its own patch of ground on the horizon.
